answer: Shared-seed continuity proof. Each identity derives its keypair from a kernel held in a hardware vault; every signed action emits a rotating beacon value chained to prior actions. A duplicate identity, cloned from the same seed, produces two diverging beacon chains that any auditor reconciles against the vault's monotonic counter, revealing the fork on first conflicting emission. An attacker must provision a distinct physical vault and kernel per identity, paying full hardware and key-ceremony cost each time.
